C05 and C11 are related anniversary-observance models, but their operative structures are less closely aligned with the child.","shared_material":[{"child_excerpt":"I call upon all agencies and officials of the Federal Government, upon the Governors of the States, and upon the officers of local governments to encourage and facilitate the suitable observance of this occasion.","parent_excerpt":"I request the appropriate officials of the Federal Government and of the several States, Territories, possessions, and municipalities of the United States to cooperate in the preparation for, and observance of, that year.","explanation":"Both provisions enlist corresponding federal, state, and local governmental actors to facilitate an officially designated observance."},{"child_excerpt":"I also urge all citizens to participate in appropriate activities and ceremonies","parent_excerpt":"I also urge business, labor, agricultural, educational, and civic groups, as well as the people of the United States generally, to observe 1960 ... with exhibits, ceremonies, and other appropriate activities","explanation":"The later proclamation closely follows C08’s separate public-participation clause, including “I also urge,” ceremonies, and appropriate activities."},{"child_excerpt":"this treaty has resulted in collaboration ... and has thereby significantly contributed to economic, social, and cultural progress","parent_excerpt":"travel is an important element in the development of greater international understanding and thus tends to promote international peace","explanation":"Each proclamation frames the observance as advancing international cooperation and peace, reinforcing the parallel operative drafting."}]}
